summary.headline: Dollar Industries Q4 FY26 operating income rose 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore, but EBITDA grew only 2.0% as gross margin fell to 28.1%; price hikes of ~4-6% announced for FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income grew 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore on 12.0% volume growth, while gross margin fell about 169 bps to 28.1% due to a shift to the economy range (47% of revenue vs 45%) and higher cotton and yarn prices. Operating EBITDA rose 2.0% to INR58 crore (9.3% margin) and PAT rose 11.4% to INR33 crore. For FY26, operating income grew 10.0% to INR1,881 crore, PAT rose 18.0% to INR107 crore, and operating cash flow was INR139 crore. Management implemented a calibrated price hike in Q1 FY27 (about 3-4% in April and a further 2-3% from June) and began the Phase 2 pilot of Project Lakshya. No formal FY27 guidance was given; it is due with the Q1 call.

financial_highlights.change: gross profit +6.7% YoY; margin down ~169 bps YoY

segments.name: Economy range (Dollar Always)
segments.commentary: Contributed 47% of Q4 FY26 revenue vs 45% in Q4 FY25 and about 41% for FY26 (FY25: 39.1%); management attributes the rise to demand in Tier 2/3 and rural areas, not structural change.

segments.name: Dollar Man / Big Boss (mid-premium flagship)
segments.commentary: Contributed 36.5% of FY26 revenue vs 38.8% in FY25; Regular and Big Boss together anchor the portfolio at 41.5% and 36.5% respectively.

segments.name: Force NXT (super premium)
segments.commentary: Value +16.0% and volume +24.3% in Q4; FY26 value +16.5% and volume +26.2%; 4.5% share of revenue vs 4.2% in FY25.

segments.name: Dollar Protect (rainwear)
segments.commentary: Volume +49.9% in Q4 and +18% for FY26; 2.1% of revenue.

segments.name: Missy (women) / Thermals
segments.commentary: Missy 7.5% of revenue (8.0% in FY25); Thermals 6.1% (5.9% in FY25). Dollar Socks 1.6%.

segments.name: Quick commerce / modern trade / e-commerce
segments.commentary: Quick commerce grew 437% YoY and rose from 0.5% to 2.5% of revenue; non-traditional channels grew 24.2% in FY26. Trade channel is about 87% of sales, e-commerce and quick commerce about 10%, exports about 3%.

segments.name: G.O.A.T alliance
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR49 crore (+45% YoY) and PAT INR4.9 crore (about 10% margin).

segments.name: Pepe Inner Fashion JV
segments.commentary: Licensed Pepe Jeans athleisure innerwear, D2C-focused; 51% owned by Dollar (2% non-voting). Only bottom line is consolidated, so JV revenue is excluded from top line.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance; management will give firm full-year guidance with the Q1 FY27 call.
Management expects FY27 margins to be better than FY26 (FY26 EBITDA margin about 10.8%, per management) and is eyeing double-digit growth in volume and value.
Price hikes of about 4-6% total (3-4% in April, 2-3% more from June); CFO cited 6-7% in one answer. Management says no further hikes are needed as cotton and yarn prices stabilise.
Targets a further 5-7 day cut in the cash conversion cycle in FY27, mainly from receivable days.
Debt of about INR264 crore expected to be reduced, with the CFO saying debt can go to zero by FY28.
Modern trade channel expected to grow 20-25% in FY27.
Merger with promoter companies (NCLT first motion obtained) expected to save INR4-5 crore in royalty, service charges and rent; revenue impact small.
capex_capacity: No major capex planned in the near term; garment capacity can be flexed 20-30% by adding job workers, with about 28 crore pieces produced in FY26.
Knitting, bleaching and cutting are in-house; stitching is largely outsourced to job workers, mainly for economy and mix segments.
Inventory days fell from about 130 to 100; management sees about 95-100 days as the optimised level given the roughly 90-day production cycle and SKU count.
Project Lakshya Phase 2 pilot started in strong 'gold' states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Mumbai and surroundings); non-Lakshya state expansion is paused amid competitive pushback.
Exports go mainly to the Gulf, parts of Africa and Myanmar.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand was affected by exceptional heat, which reduced retail footfall; management calls it timing rather than structural, and says underlying demand is intact.
Price hike did not dent demand per management; they expect no market share loss as organized peers take the hike at the same time.
Competitive intensity is described as stabilising; management says D2C brands moving back online had only a minor impact on offline share.
Economy range demand was stronger than mid-premium in Q4 (down-trading called rare by management); Force NXT grew 25-26%.
Gross margin compression blamed mainly on mix (economy share up) and higher yarn prices that were not passed through until April.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the price hike was taken, when, and is more coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry hike came after about 2 years. About 3-4% was taken in April and 2-3% more from June, so about 4-6% in total with no scheme rollback, and management sees no further hikes needed.

qa_highlights.question: Can debt of INR264 crore be paid down quickly, and what guidance is there for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt can be reduced to zero by FY28; INR50 crore of borrowings was already cut last year. Firm FY27 guidance will come with the Q1 call; management is optimistic on volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin decline is cotton versus competition or discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it mainly to mix (economy segment at 47%) and higher yarn prices that were not passed through; management cited no competition-led discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the shift to economy products structural or down-trading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said down-trading is rare and the shift is temporary, driven by Tier 2/3 and rural demand, with some unorganised-to-organised shift and Dollar Lehar advertising.

qa_highlights.question: Will double-digit revenue growth and margins above FY26 be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will be better and double-digit growth is targeted, but declined to quantify revenue growth until the Q1 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Lakshya contribution trend and expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly Lakshya figures are not meaningful because it is secondary sales; the full-year contribution is similar to last year. Expansion into new states is paused until Phase 2 is proven.

risks_watch: Gross margin: Q4 margin down ~169 bps, with EBITDA growth only 2%; watch whether the April-June price hikes restore margin in Q1 FY27.
Management has not given FY27 numeric guidance; the Q1 call is the next checkpoint.
Pricing answers were inconsistent (4-6% in one answer, 6-7% in another), so the actual realisation uplift needs verification.
Receivable days reduction (the main working capital lever) and the 5-7 day cash conversion target.
Weak Q4 footfall from heat; Q1 is seasonally important for innerwear demand.
Lakshya Phase 2 pilot outcomes and whether non-Lakshya state entry resumes.
Merger execution and the NCLT process for the promoter companies.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and cash generation, but cautious and sometimes vague on specifics: management declined to quantify FY27 revenue growth or margins, deferring them to the Q1 call. Gross margin pressure was acknowledged openly. Some answers were muddled by line breaks and repeated phrasing.
key_quotes: Our net cash from operating activities as a proportion of Operating EBITDA stood at 70% as of 31st March 2026, affirming that our reported profits are backed by real cash generation.
So the price hike that we have taken in the Q1, I think we don't have to take any further price hike now.
It's not a structural thing which is happening. It's a very temporary thing.
But overall, we are very optimistic and hopeful for a great fiscal year, FY27.

growth.why: No formal FY27 numeric guidance; management is 'very hopeful' of double-digit volume and value growth, backed mainly by 4-6% price hikes and demand/share gains, with no specific capacity or order numbers, and firm guidance is due with Q1 FY27.
